note: Real briefs, not smoke tests: each is a package somebody would actually have to hand to a reviewer, chosen for the specific way a study package goes wrong while looking finished — a number typed from the conversation rather than rendered from a result, a stale result quietly dropped, an unreviewed package labelled as a specified analysis. mustDo / mustNotDo are the rubric; the deterministic half (the files at their names, every prose number present in results.json, the four counts apart, the two seal timestamps) is the vcr-study-package contract in @evimed/domain, whose findings are notices and never a gate (the capability ships no preflight script of its own).

briefs.title: EV-201 二线 NSCLC：设计支持用途的研究包
briefs.why: The ordinary full case and the one AC-20 was written for. Every number in this package exists as a saved result; the failure that looks like success is a well-written report whose figures were retyped from the conversation and are one revision out of date.
mustDo: Write every number as a {{n:…}} reference into results.json and let the platform render it.
Ship all nine sections in order: summary, input register, assumption register, population and comparator definitions, results, figures, execution record, validation and limits, decision record.
State the review status on the cover exactly as it is, including 「未复核」, and say what intended use the package may therefore claim.
State the four counts apart wherever a sample size appears.
Name the kind of every interval printed.
Record the seed, software versions and CPU seconds of every execution in the execution record.
Say that the intended use is design_support and what would be needed to raise it.
mustNotDo: Type any number into the prose instead of referencing it.
Claim 「指定研究分析」 for an unreviewed package.
Describe retrieval or tooling in the report body ('I searched…', a tool name, a job id).
Present a Monte-Carlo interval as a confidence interval.
Leave out a result because it is inconvenient.
briefs.gradedOn: Whether a reviewer could recompute every figure in the package from results.json without asking a question.

briefs.title: 结论是「不可估计」的研究包：外部对照不可行，要写清楚缺什么
briefs.why: A finished result that reads like a failure (plan §3.6). Packages of this kind are routinely written as apologies or quietly re-scoped into a different question; the right shape states the deterministic rule that fired, the gaps, and what the study can still answer.
mustDo: Present the not-estimable verdict as the study's result, with the deterministic rule that fired named.
List the gaps: what data is missing, how much of it, and what becomes possible once it exists.
Say what the study can still answer at its current data tier.
Keep every computed diagnostic that led to the verdict in the results section — overlap, standardized differences, effective sample size.
Write the limits section about the comparison, not about the platform.
mustNotDo: Re-scope the question so that something estimable can be reported instead.
Present a sensitivity analysis as if it were the primary estimate.
Write 「数据不足」 without saying which fields, for how many patients, over which window.
Apologise instead of reporting.
briefs.gradedOn: Whether a sponsor reading it would know exactly what to collect next, and whether the verdict is stated as a result rather than as an error.

briefs.title: CDE 沟通交流资料包：确证性用途，含结局封存的两个时间戳
briefs.why: The regulatory-facing case. The thing a reviewer looks for first is whether the analysis plan was fixed before anyone saw the outcomes, and a package that asserts it without the two timestamps is asserting what it cannot show.
mustDo: Print the analysis-plan freeze time with its hash and the first outcome-field read time, in that order, in the validation section.
Organise the pack by the CDE real-world-evidence communication guidance: necessity and feasibility, data suitability, protocol and statistical analysis plan, bias control and sensitivity analyses.
State the review status of each kind (clinical, statistical, data) with the version each countersigned.
Report any stale result: either recomputed, or stated as stale on the cover with its reason.
State the intended-use ceiling the model evidence supports and why, if it is lower than the one requested.
mustNotDo: Claim the plan was pre-specified without the two timestamps.
Drop a stale result from the package.
Label the package 「申报准备」 when the model evidence or the review status does not support it.
Rewrite a number to match a sentence.
briefs.gradedOn: Whether a regulatory reviewer could establish the order of plan freeze and outcome access from the package alone.

briefs.title: EV-201 外部对照：冻结前的模型分析计划，一个模型还没有评估记录
briefs.why: The plan is frozen before the data are opened, so the words around it are the part a run can get wrong without anyone noticing: a section that rewrites the platform's assessment table in softer language, one that quietly reports a result, or one that fills a model's missing assessment with a plausible rating. The tables, hashes and gaps are the platform's; the failure that looks like success is a fluent plan that has stopped saying what it lacks.
mustDo: Read what the platform wrote first (vcr_read report_model with filter.kind model_analysis_plan) and write only introduction, objectives, data and methods, once each.
Say in the methods words which model has no assessment record and what the plan therefore does not yet state, rather than leaving the table's 「未填写」 unexplained.
Write any number a section needs as a {{n:…}} reference.
Describe the evaluation approach (verification, validation, applicability) the technical criteria will be held to, in terms the assessment records already state.
mustNotDo: Rewrite, soften or contradict a rating, a model risk or its stated rule in the platform's assessment table.
Report or anticipate any result: the plan is written before the analysis.
Invent an assessment record, a rating or a technical criterion for the model that lacks one.
Submit a section other than the four, or the same section twice with different claims.
Name the freeze, the hash or the version as if the words were part of what was frozen.
briefs.gradedOn: Whether a regulator reading the plan could tell, from the words alone, which parts of the plan are decided, which are not yet written, and that no result has been seen.

briefs.title: EV-201 外部对照：模型分析报告，计划冻结后假设变了一处，一个结果不可估计
briefs.why: The report is where a changed assumption and an unestimable result are most tempting to smooth over. The platform lists every deviation from the frozen plan and prints 「不可估计」 with its rule; the run's discussion is the only place the reasons live, and a report that says nothing about a listed deviation, or fills the unestimable result with a figure, is exactly the work that reads as finished.
mustDo: Read modelAnalysis.plan, modelAnalysis.deviations and modelAnalysis.results before writing, and write the seven sections that are the run's, once each.
Explain in the discussion why each listed deviation happened and what it changes about the results; if the reason is not in the study's records, say it is not recorded.
Write the not-estimable result as a finished result: the rule that triggered it, what is missing, what would make it estimable.
Reference every number as {{n:modelAnalysis.results[i].measures[j]…}} or another saved field; never retype one.
mustNotDo: Leave a listed deviation unexplained or describe it as a change to the plan.
Offer an estimate, a range or a 「大约」 for the result the engine declared not estimable.
Claim the analysis followed the plan when the platform lists deviations, or invent a plan when none was frozen.
Write under the appendices or restate the platform's tables in prose with different numbers.
Raise the intended use above what the results' own labels allow.
briefs.gradedOn: Whether every deviation the platform lists has a stated reason in the discussion, and whether the not-estimable result is carried as a conclusion and not as a failure.
